Definition: a prolonged form of a compound probably of a derivative of the base of G1476 and perhaps G2192; properly, keeping one's seat (sedentary), i.e. (by implication) still (undisturbed, undisturbing):--peaceable, quiet.
BiblicalUsage: hēsýchios means peaceable, quiet. It turns up twice, in 1 Timothy and 1 Peter.
TheologicalSignificance: My position is simple here: hēsýchios means peaceable, quiet, and I do not stretch it further.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
